newsitem.title: new Zealand: NZ shares end sharply lower, all leaders down.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end sharply lower, all leaders down.

text.p: New Zealand share prices ended sharply lower on Monday on higher-than-normal turnover, which suggested the sale of part of a large portfolio, brokers said.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 31.76 points down at 2,190.26 on turnover worth NZ$62 million.
All leading stocks were weaker, most notably Telecom, down 13 cents at NZ$6.72, and Carter Holt Harvey, down 13 at $3.15.
"There was a large seller in the market, so it looks like a large exit from a portfolio, maybe pre-election," Duncan Rutherford at ANZ Securities said.
"I suppose to that extent, news that the (governing) National Party had gained ground in the polls and that (opposition party) New Zealand First had lost ground went largely unnoticed," he said.
An election is due on October 12.
Brokers had earlier held out some hope of some end-of-quarter buying, but there was no follow-through.
TransAlta New Zealand had a successful debut, ending at NZ$1.65, off its peak of $1.70 but up sharply from its first traded price of $1.55.
TransAlta NZ, New Zealand's fourth largest electricity supply company, is the product of a merger between Wellington's EnergyDirect and Capital Power.
Canada's TransAlta Corp has a 63 percent interest in the merged group.
